extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, LTCHs, organ procurement organizations (OPOs) and histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), Medicare providers, and Medicare payment policy stakeholders/analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and explains the proposed payment, reporting, and quality-measure policies and the methodologies CMS used to model FY2027 impacts for the IPPS, capital IPPS, excluded hospitals, and the LTCH PPS, including information collection burden estimates and proposed quality reporting changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPO/HCL information collection burden (Form CMS-216-94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden hours for each OPO/HCL are the estimated time required to complete ongoing data gathering and recordkeeping tasks, search existing data resources, review instructions, and complete OMB number 0938-0102, Form CMS-216-94. Currently 94 Medicare certified OPOs/HCLs file Form CMS-216-94 annually. The current estimated average burden per OPO/HCL is 45 hours (30 hours for recordkeeping and 15 hours for reporting). For this proposal, CMS estimates no additional recordkeeping burden but an average additional reporting burden of 10 hours per OPO/HCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS used Bureau of Labor Statistics median hourly wage for Category 13-2011 of $39.27, added 100% for fringe/overhead to get $78.54/hour, multiplied by 10 hours to estimate $785.40 additional annual reporting cost per OPO/HCL and $73,828 total (94 × $785.40). CMS recognizes variation by size/complexity and invites public comment on the hours estimate and staffing requirements; because of a proposed 1-year delay, estimated costs would not occur until FY 2028.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized definitions and accounting practices (42 CFR 413.20(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 42 CFR 413.20(a), CMS follows standardized definitions, accounting, statistics, and reporting practices that are widely accepted in the healthcare industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in these practices and systems are not required to determine costs payable under the principles of reimbursement; methods use data available from the institution's basis accounts, as usually maintained, to arrive at equitable and proper payment for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for determining Medicare costs payable
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods of determining costs payable under Medicare involve making use of data available from the institution's basis accounts, as usually maintained, to arrive at equitable and proper payment for services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes reliance on existing institution accounting records and reporting practices rather than requiring changes in practices to determine reimbursable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of the Reasonable Cost Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to change existing policy and to codify longstanding Medicare reasonable cost reimbursement policies, applicable to all providers reimbursed on a reasonable cost basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes these proposals would not result in additional costs to Medicare or increased burden on providers, may alleviate burden by clarifying cost reporting policies, and could result in cost savings due to increased payment accuracy although insufficient data exist to estimate an amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to codify cost allocation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to codify cost allocation principles applicable to all providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes no additional costs to the Medicare program would result because providers are already required to follow current cost reporting instructions; proposals may yield payment accuracy improvements but estimates are not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codify discretionary Administrator review for appeals under §413.420(g) for IOPOs and HCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to codify the discretionary Administrator review of CMS reviewing official determinations with respect to appeals under §413.420(g) for Independent Organ Procurement Organizations (IOPOs) and Histocompatibility Laboratories (HCLs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects no additional costs to Medicare and no increased burden on providers as a result of this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections/clarifications to regulatory text (§412.116(c) and §413.404(b)(3)(ii)(A) and (C))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed technical corrections or clarifications to regulation text at §§412.116(c) and 413.404(b)(3)(ii)(A) and (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clarifications and corrections would not create any additional costs to the Medicare program or increased burden upon providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate‑of‑increase limit update for hospitals excluded from IPPS (§413.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: For hospitals paid on a reasonable cost basis subject to the rate-of-increase ceiling under §413.40, the update of the rate-of-increase limit (target amount) is the estimated proposed FY 2027 percentage increase in the 2023-based IPPS operating market basket (estimated at 3.2 percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded hospitals paid under §413.40 are not subject to the productivity reduction required under section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(I) and therefore the update for those hospitals is the market basket percentage increase (3.2% in CMS's estimate). The impact on excluded hospitals depends on cumulative cost increases since base period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess cost payment rule for excluded hospitals (§413.40(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §413.40(d)(3), an excluded hospital paid under TEFRA whose costs exceed 110 percent of its rate-of-increase limit receives its rate-of-increase limit plus the lesser of: (1) 50 percent of its reasonable costs in excess of 110 percent of the limit; or (2) 10 percent of its limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, hospitals may obtain payment adjustments for justifiable increases in operating costs that exceed the limit under various provisions of §413.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital IPPS payment methodology (§412.312 formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic methodology for calculating capital IPPS payments: (Standard Federal rate) × (DRG weight) × (GAF) × (COLA for hospitals located in Alaska and Hawaii) × (1 + DSH adjustment factor + IME adjustment factor, if applicable). Hospitals may receive outlier payments for qualifying cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes a capital Federal rate update of 3.1 percent and applied additional budget neutrality and adjustment factors (see separate entries). Payment modeling multiplies capital Federal rate by geographic adjustment factor and case-mix, then adds IME, DSH, and outlier estimates where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital IPPS payment model assumptions and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact analysis used December 2025 updates of the FY 2025 MedPAR file and Provider-Specific File (PSF) and most recently available hospital cost report data to categorize hospitals. Short-term acute care hospitals not paid under general IPPS (e.g., hospitals in Maryland) were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes interdependent nature of IPPS makes precise attribution difficult, uses best available sources, and acknowledges some hospitals may be misclassified due to data variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAF/DRG budget neutrality and capital adjustment factors
rubrics_metrics.description: In calculating the proposed FY 2027 capital Federal rate CMS applied a GAF/DRG budget neutrality adjustment factor of 1.0139, a proposed budget neutrality factor for the 5-percent cap on wage index decreases and continuation of transition for discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy of 0.9913, and a proposed outlier adjustment factor of 0.9642.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These multiplicative factors adjust the FY 2027 capital Federal rate; together with the 3.1% update they drive the modeled change in capital payments per case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassification effects on wage index and GAF (MGCRB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals may apply for reclassification for wage index purposes under section 1886(d)(10) (MGCRB). Reclassification affects the wage index and thus the geographic adjustment factor (GAF), impacting capital payments per case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS modeled reclassified vs non-reclassified hospitals and reported expected percent changes (e.g., urban reclassified +2.4% vs urban non-reclassified +2.1%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment simulation reporting dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of estimated payments per case for FY 2026 and proposed FY 2027 provided by: (1) geographic location; (2) region; and (3) payment classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present columns for FY 2026 estimate, FY 2027 estimate, and percentage change (which includes the 3.1% update and other changes). CMS used a universe of 3,013 hospitals for the capital IPPS simulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual‑rate LTCH PPS payment structure (site neutral vs standard Federal payment rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(m)(6)(A) establishes a dual rate LTCH PPS structure: LTCH discharges that meet statutory patient-level criteria for exclusion from the site neutral payment rate are paid based on the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate; discharges that do not meet exclusion criteria are paid the site neutral payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site neutral payment rate is the lower of the IPPS comparable per diem amount (as determined under §412.529(d)(4), including applicable outlier payments, reduced by 4.6% for FYs 2018–2026) or 100% of the estimated cost of the case (as determined under §412.529(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH per discharge payment methodology (§§412.515–412.533 and 412.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic methodology for determining per discharge payment for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases includes adjustment by the MS‑LTC‑DRG relative weight, area wage levels, short stay outliers (SSOs), and COLA for Alaska and Hawaii; HCO payments may also apply when thresholds are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment components and adjustments mirror IPPS-like mechanics tailored to LTCHs; HCO payments apply to both standard rate and site neutral cases when thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate and QRP penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes an LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate of $52,177.04 reflecting a proposed 2.4 percent annual update and a budget neutrality factor for area wage adjustment of 1.0025505. For LTCHs that fail to submit LTCH QRP data, CMS proposes a standard Federal rate of $51,157.95 reflecting the required 2.0 percentage point reduction to the annual update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required LTCH QRP data triggers a 2.0 percentage point reduction to the annual update per section 1886(m)(5)(C) of the Act; the proposed standard rates reflect these adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor‑related share for LTCHs (73.0%)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to establish a labor-related share of 73.0 percent for LTCHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposal is based on IGI's fourth quarter 2025 forecast of the relative importance of the labor-related share of operating and capital costs of the 2022-based LTCH market basket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index update methodology for LTCHs
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes updating wage index values for LTCHs based on most recent available data (data from cost reporting periods beginning during FY 2023), the same data used for the FY 2027 IPPS wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These wage index updates feed into area wage level adjustments and affect LTCH payments via the labor-related share and related budget neutrality factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: COLA factors for Alaska and Hawaii using DOD OCOLA
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to update the COLA factors used to adjust non-labor related costs for LTCHs located in Alaska and Hawaii using the Overseas Cost-of-Living Allowance (OCOLA) data published by the Department of Defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These updated COLA factors adjust non-labor portions of LTCH payments for geographic cost differences in AK/HI.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS‑LTC‑DRG classifications, relative weights, fixed‑loss and outlier assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to update MS‑LTC‑DRG classifications and relative weights, and to maintain the fixed-loss amount at $78,936, estimating outlier payments equal to 7.975 percent of estimated FY 2027 payments for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS models outlier payments based on the fixed-loss amount and expects outliers to represent ~7.975% of payments; updates to DRG classifications and weights affect case-level payment calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH impact analysis simulation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate per discharge payment effects CMS simulated FY 2026 and proposed FY 2027 payments on a case-by-case basis using historical LTCH claims from FY 2025 MedPAR files that met or would have met LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate criteria. In modeling HCO cases, CMS scaled outlier payments to equal 7.975% of total estimated LTCH PPS payments for standard Federal payment rate cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis included 318 LTCHs (excluded all‑inclusive rate providers and two LTCHs that only had site neutral cases). Based on the FY2025 cases used, ~7% were site neutral cases and ~93% would meet exclusion criteria for the standard Federal payment rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH impact reporting classifications and table columns (Table IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: LTCHs in impact tables are grouped by Location (large urban/other urban/rural), Ownership control (voluntary/proprietary/government), Census region, and Bed size (0–24, 25–49, 50–74, 75–124, >125). Table IV columns display: LTCH Classification, number of LTCHs, number of cases expected to meet standard Federal payment rate criteria, estimated FY 2026 payment per discharge, estimated FY 2027 payment per discharge, percent change due to annual update, percent change due to area wage adjustment and budget neutrality, and percent change due to all changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses these groupings to present distributional effects (by geography, ownership, and size) and notes results may not reflect changes in admissions or case-mix intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary results: LTCH payment and Medicare program impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on modeled FY 2025 LTCH cases, CMS projects estimated payments per discharge for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases to increase 2.3 percent on average from FY 2026 to FY 2027. Aggregate FY 2027 payments to LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate cases are estimated at ~$2.459 billion vs ~$2.404 billion in FY 2026, an overall increase of ~$55 million for the 318 LTCHs in the database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states it believes the proposed provisions will result in appropriate Medicare payments consistent with statute and does not expect changes in quality of care or access for beneficiaries; paying prospectively should enhance efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program measure adoptions, modifications, and removals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals include adopting: (1) Advance Care Planning eCQM (CY 2028/FY 2030); (2) Hospital Harm‑Postoperative VTE eCQM (CY 2028/FY 2030); (3) Excess Days in Acute Care After Hospitalization for Diabetes measure (July 1, 2025–June 30, 2027 performance period, associated with FY 2029). Also proposing to adopt five mortality measures for specified performance periods and to modify three Excess Days in Acute Care measures. Proposed removals: VTE Prophylaxis eCQM, Intensive Care Unit VTE Prophylaxis eCQM, Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy eCQM. Propose updates to Maternal Morbidity Structural measure reporting/submission beginning CY 2026/FY 2028, require mandatory reporting of Malnutrition Care Score eCQM (CY 2028/FY 2030), and require mandatory reporting of Hospital Harm eCQMs after 2 years of self-selected reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes replacing two process eCQMs with a single comprehensive outcome eCQM would reduce administrative burden; Hospital Harm-Postoperative VTE eCQM would become mandatory if the proposal to require Hospital Harm eCQMs after two years of self-selected reporting is finalized. Timing and phased adoption periods are specified for each measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection burden estimates for proposed HQR policies
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS estimates an increase of 8,133 hours at a cost of $447,803 in information collection burden associated with the proposed policies compared to currently approved estimates under OMB control number 0938-1022 (expiration December 31, 2028).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains some proposals (e.g., replacing two VTE process eCQMs with one Hospital Harm outcome eCQM) will not change burden because hospitals could already self-select those measures, but could reduce administrative burden overall. Detailed Collection of Information burdens for mandatory Hospital Harm reporting are provided elsewhere (section XII.B.4.g.).
